what_its_for: Olsalazine is used to keep ulcerative colitis from flaring up (coming back) in people who cannot take another medicine called sulfasalazine. It helps reduce swelling and irritation in your large intestine (colon).
how_to_take: Take olsalazine capsules by mouth WITH FOOD. Taking it with food is very important because it greatly reduces the chance of diarrhea, which is a common side effect. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg (one capsule) taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, both times with a meal. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still close to the time you were supposed to take it. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store olsalazine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking olsalazine if you are allergic to aspirin or other salicylate medicines, as this drug is related to aspirin. Be careful with blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin) — olsalazine may increase their effects and raise your bleeding risk, so tell your doctor if you take them. Avoid taking antacids or other medications at the same time without checking with your pharmacist, as they may affect how this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe or worsening diarrhea or stomach pain; bloody diarrhea; signs of a kidney problem such as changes in how much you urinate, swelling in your legs, or blood in your urine; signs of liver problems like yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness; chest pain or shortness of breath; a skin rash, hives, or itching; fever, joint pain, or flu-like symptoms; unusual bruising or bleeding. Also call your doctor if your ulcerative colitis symptoms get worse or do not improve.
when_it_works: Olsalazine starts working in your colon within a few days, but it may take several weeks before you notice the full benefit. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because it is working to prevent your symptoms from coming back. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may pass into breast milk. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Children: Safety and dosing in children has not been well established — ask your child's doctor for guidance. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects; your doctor will monitor you carefully.
